newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products steady, tenders talked.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products steady, tenders talked.

text.p: The Singapore oil products market returned on Friday from its two-day break with levels unchanged in very thin trading, traders said.
Most traders were still out of the market and were not expected to return in full force until Monday, when Japan also returns from a week-long holiday, traders said.

A major offered 30,000 tonnes of gas oil lifting January 18-22 at $32.45 per barrel fob Singapore, much firmer than the $31.95 sales on Tuesday -- the last trading day. Swaps opened firmer at $32.10/$32.35 on the back of firmer IPE gas oil, but drifted later to $32.00/$32.25.

Jet fuel was bid at $32.70 per barrel for 100,000 barrels lifting January 29-February 2, down from Tuesday's bid at $33.50. A seller emerged with 150,000 barrels but far apart at $33.95 and for January 20-24 lifting. The Jan jet/gas oil spread widened to $2.40/$2.50 from $2.20/2.50 on Tuesday.

Sri Lanka's 45-day maintenance shutdown of its 50,000-60,000 barrel-per-day refinery in mid-January saw it issue its third diesel/jet fuel tender and one diesel/gasoline tender for the month. It awarded its second buy tender for mid-January arrival gas oil and jet fuel to trader BB Energy at $1.57 and $1.77 per barrel respectively, over Singapore quotes, c-and-f Colombo.

Traders said Taiwan only took one leaded and unleaded 95-octane reformate cargo from a Dutch trader at above $27.10 per barrel and a Japanese trader at $27.00 respectively. Some said the awards were on the slightly low side considering the high freight costs.

Some traders were bearish saying the only other regional gasoline demand was from India which was seeking a 25,000 tonne cargo of 87-octane leaded gasoline for January 16-31 delivery to Kandla/Goa in a tender which closes January 9.
